_README: This is the single source of the book's structure. The build is driven ENTIRELY by this file. Fill in every field, delete the _comment/_README keys or leave them (the builder ignores unknown keys). Chapter ids MUST start with 'ch' (ch01, ch02, ...). A chapter is treated as translated once out/<id>_reading.md exists. Cite the book's own PRINTED FOLIO in notes, never the PDF page.
_translator_note: Optional. A list of paragraph strings rendered verbatim as the Translator's Note back-matter page. Inline ... is honored; use NUMERIC character references (— em dash,   nbsp), never named entities. If omitted, a generic method note is generated.
translator_note: This is an English translation of 中文書名, from an image-only scan with no digital text layer.

Say here how the text was recovered and verified, what the register decisions were, who the author is and how to read the source, and how any damaged or missing passages were handled. Keep it honest about method and provenance.
_source_note: Free-text provenance: where the scan came from, how many PDF pages, seal/artifact warnings, whether the PDF has bookmarks. Informational only.
source_note: Image-only PDF scan; NN pages; no text layer. Note any library seal, dark-edge artifacts, or embedded bookmarks here.
_offset_note: The PDF-page-to-printed-folio offset usually DRIFTS as unpaginated plates accumulate. Do NOT use a constant formula. Record per-section pdf_page/printed_page anchors below and READ the folio off the scan at each opener.
_structure_note: One entry per chapter. Each chapter: id (ch01..), chapter (int), title (zh), title_en, pdf_page + printed_page of its opener, and a sections list. Each section: id (ch01s01..), section (int), title (zh), title_en, pdf_page, printed_page. The reading markdown uses '## ' for the chapter (h1), '### ' for each section (h2, matched to these ids in order), '#### ' for subsections (h3).
_batches_note: Your work plan: split the book into batches (a chapter, or a run of sections) and do each end to end. Informational, but keeping it here lets a fresh session see the plan. first_section/last_section are section ids.
_back_matter_note: Optional. If the book has a publisher's errata table or a colophon you want reproduced as translator's back matter, put the data in back_matter.json (see that file). This list is just a human record of what exists.
